Issues.Title: test(compiler-cli): mark @boundary content projection diagnostic as known ngp failure
Issues.Body:
Add the newly introduced control flow content projection diagnostic spec for `@boundary` blocks to `NGP_KNOWN_NGTSC_FAILURES`, pending implementation in the NGP compiler backend.

This unblocks CI on `main` where `//packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc:ngtsc_ngp` failed following the merge of #71289.

Issues.Title: docs: match the DI error samples to the runtime messages
Issues.Body:
The NG0201, NG0200 and NG0203 samples on the DI troubleshooting page show
wording Angular no longer prints. They also start the path at `App`, which
never appears in a path built from the environment injector.

Use the current messages and start each path at the first injected service.
The four `{{user().name}}` templates read a plain object field, so they
become `{{user.name}}`.

In the hierarchical injection guide, the projected `<app-inspector>` gets
🐳 from the root-provided `AnimalService`, not from `App`'s `viewProviders`.
`App` has no `viewProviders` in that example.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: match the DI error samples to the runtime messages" (#71365)

## What is the current behavior?

`inject(Dir, {host: true})` (or `@Host()`) returns null in a component that is nested in its own template, from the second level of nesting on. The `@Host` boundary check also compares the LView that contains the declaration component's host element, so the lookup only stops at the real host element. Added an acceptance test in `di_spec.ts` with a component nested three levels deep. It fails on main (levels 3 and 4 get null) and passes with the fix.

- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(router): respect guard order when a guard throws a RedirectCommand
Issues.Body:
Guards in the same array resolve in array order: the first guard that does not return `true` decides the result, even if a later guard finishes first. A guard that threw a `RedirectCommand` skipped this, because the thrown error ended the combined guard result immediately, so its redirect won over an earlier guard that was still running.

Treat a thrown `RedirectCommand` as that guard's result, like a returned one. Other errors still fail the navigation.

Fixes #71357

Issues.Title: A guard that throws a RedirectCommand takes priority over earlier guards in the same array
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Since 22.2, guards can throw a `RedirectCommand` instead of returning it. When a guard throws, its redirect wins
even if an earlier guard in the same array is still running and also redirects.

```ts
{path: 'admin', component: Admin, canActivate: [isLoggedIn, hasPlan]}
```

- `isLoggedIn` is async and returns `new RedirectCommand(parseUrl('/login'))`.
- `hasPlan` throws `new RedirectCommand(parseUrl('/upgrade'))`.

Expected: `/login`. The [guards guide](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards#applying-guards-to-routes)
says "the router uses the result of the first guard in the array that did not return `true`, even if a later guard
finished earlier". Returning the same `RedirectCommand` from `hasPlan` instead of throwing it gives `/login`.

Actual: `/upgrade`.

The guards' results are combined with `combineLatest` in `prioritizedGuardValue`, which errors as soon as one guard
throws, before the earlier guards have finished.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://stackblitz.com/edit/ptesajgk?file=src%2Fmain.ts

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
No error. The navigation redirects to the wrong URL.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 22.2.2 (@angular/router 22.2.2)
Browser: Chrome
```

### Anything else?

I have a fix with a spec ready: a thrown `RedirectCommand` is treated as that guard's result, so the guard order
applies to it like a returned one. Other errors still fail the navigation.

Issues.Title: feat(language-service): complete object literal keys in templates
Issues.Body:
Previously, the cursor within a key of an object literal in a template expression was treated as a regular expression position, so the language service suggested the component scope (members and keywords) instead of the keys of the object literal's contextual type, e.g. for `[input]="[{he}]"` where the input expects `Array<{height?: number}>`. An empty object literal produced no completions at all.

The keys of object literals are generated in the TCB as quoted string literals that carry the key's source span, so the completion request can be delegated to TypeScript at the corresponding location in the TCB, where contextual typing provides the correct member completions for object literals in any position (single objects, arrays, nested literals). Properties that are already present in the literal are excluded, and the typed key prefix is replaced via the completion replacement span.

Fixes #66357

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): compare temporaries in ReadTemporaryExpr.isEquivalent
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows Angular's guidelines.
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (see below).
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (not applicable: no API change).

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`ReadTemporaryExpr.isEquivalent` in `template/pipeline/ir/src/expression.ts` ignores its argument:

```ts
override isEquivalent(): boolean {
  return this.xref === this.xref;
}
```

so a temporary read reports itself equivalent to any expression — a read of a different temporary, or an unrelated literal like `o.NULL_EXPR`. Every sibling IR expression checks the other operand (`e instanceof X && e.xref === this.xref`, etc.).

I haven't found a template that miscompiles because of this today; it breaks the `isEquivalent` contract that callers such as the trailing-`NULL_EXPR` trimming in `instruction.ts` rely on.

## What is the new behavior?

`isEquivalent` returns true only for a `ReadTemporaryExpr` of the same temporary, matching the sibling expressions.

## Tests

Added `packages/compiler/test/template/pipeline/expression_spec.ts` with three cases (same temporary, different temporary, unrelated expression). Before the fix the last two fail with `Expected true to be false`; after the fix all three pass.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>WebMCP-org/npm-packages (@​mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill)</summary>

### [`v6.0.2`](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/blob/HEAD/packages/webmcp-polyfill/CHANGELOG.md#602)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/compare/@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6.0.1...@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6.0.2)

### [`v6.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/blob/HEAD/packages/webmcp-polyfill/CHANGELOG.md#601)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/compare/@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6.0.0...@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6.0.1)

### [`v6.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/blob/HEAD/packages/webmcp-polyfill/CHANGELOG.md#600)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/compare/@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@5.1.0...@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6.0.0)

##### Major Changes

- [`160acc3`](https://redirect.github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/commit/160acc3): **Breaking: replace the MCP-B core implementation with the upstream WebMCP polyfill.**
  Declarative tools remain available until upstream supports them.
  This package vendors [upstream revision `6bf6c57`](https://redirect.github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp-polyfill/tree/6bf6c57bbaf3d1173d7737cfb79572632d9b7871)
  and uses `webmcp-types@0.1.9` for the browser contract.

  The existing package name remains available as a temporary compatibility alias.
  It will eventually be removed; no removal date is set. Sites using declarative
  tools should keep it until the upstream polyfill supports them. Follow the
  [official upstream installation instructions](https://redirect.github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp-polyfill#readme)
  when migrating to its distribution. Until that release is available, keep using
  `@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill` with the changes below.

##### Replace initialization and cleanup

```diff
- import { initializeWebMCPPolyfill } from '@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill';
- initializeWebMCPPolyfill({ installTestingShim: true });
+ import { installWebMCP } from '@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill';
+ installWebMCP();
```

`installWebMCP()` takes no options. Remove imports of `WebMCPPolyfillInitOptions`
and calls to `cleanupWebMCPPolyfill()`: the upstream context lives for the lifetime
of the document. To remove tools, pass an `AbortController`'s signal to
`registerTool(tool, { signal })` and abort that controller during cleanup. Tests
that need a completely fresh runtime should create a new page or document realm.

The `@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill/iife` export and `dist/index.iife.js` script still install
automatically. The script's global is now `WebMCPPolyfill.installWebMCP` (formerly
`WebMCPPolyfill.initializeWebMCPPolyfill`), and it ignores
`window.__webMCPPolyfillOptions`; remove that assignment. An ESM import alone does
not install the polyfill. Pin the major in CDN URLs (`@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill@6`);
pages that are not ready to migrate pin `@5` instead of `@latest`.

##### Use the document API and object input

`navigator.modelContext`, `navigator.modelContextTesting`, and the testing shim
are removed. Replace name-based testing calls and JSON-string arguments with a
descriptor from `getTools()` and an input object:

```diff
- const result = await navigator.modelContextTesting.executeTool('search', JSON.stringify({ query: 'docs' }));
+ const context = document.modelContext;
+ if (!context) throw new Error('WebMCP is unavailable');
+ const tool = (await context.getTools()).find((tool) => tool.name === 'search');
+ if (!tool) throw new Error('Search tool is unavailable');
+ const result = JSON.parse(await context.executeTool(tool, { query: 'docs' }));
```

- `executeTool()` resolves to a JSON string. Parse it once, including when the
  callback returns a string or `null`. The former unquoted-string and bare-`null`
  compatibility paths are gone.
- Return JSON-serializable values from callbacks. `undefined`, functions, cyclic
  objects, and other non-serializable results now reject instead of falling back
  to text.
- Every failed invocation rejects with `UnknownError: Tool execution failed`.
  The upstream core does not forward the reason a callback threw or rejected,
  so the former validation and execution messages are gone. Tools registered
  through `@mcp-b/global` or `BrowserMcpServer` that need to report details
  should return an error-flagged MCP result (`isError: true`) instead of throwing.
- `RegisteredTool.inputSchema` is an object when present. Remove branches that
  parse a serialized schema. Use `tool.title || tool.name` for display labels.
- Input schemas provide metadata and TypeScript inference, not runtime argument
  validation. Validate untrusted input in the callback.
- Registration signals remove tools. Use the separate
  `executeTool(tool, input, { signal })` signal to cancel an invocation, and pass
  the callback's `(input, { signal })` signal to cancellable work.

##### Move MCP-B extensions to their packages

| Previous use of the core package                                                              | Migration                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Declarative tools, `SubmitEvent.agentInvoked`, or `respondWith()`                             | Keep using this package until upstream declarative support is available.                    |
| MCP `outputSchema`, prompts, resources, or transports                                         | Use `@mcp-b/global`, or configure `BrowserMcpServer` from `@mcp-b/webmcp-ts-sdk`.           |
| `@mcp-b/webmcp-polyfill/schema`                                                               | Import schema conversion and MCP response helpers from `@mcp-b/webmcp-ts-sdk/schema`.       |
| Legacy Chrome input/result parsing, error factories, or browser-access helpers from `/schema` | Remove them; the upstream context owns browser execution, serialization, and access checks. |

`cleanupWebModelContext()` from `@mcp-b/global` removes its extensions and restores
the underlying context; it does not uninstall the core polyfill or its declarative layer.

`withAbortSignal` is removed; pass the execute callback's `signal` to cancellable
work instead.

##### Update declarative tool code

- Declarative results are JSON strings like every other `executeTool()` result.
  A string passed to `respondWith()` arrived as plain text, as in Chrome; parse it now:

  ```diff
    form.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
      event.preventDefault();
      event.respondWith?.(Promise.resolve('sent'));
    });
  - const text = await context.executeTool(tool, {});
  + const text = JSON.parse(await context.executeTool(tool, {}));
  ```

- A submission that never calls `respondWith()`, or a `respondWith()` value of
  `undefined`, resolves as `null`.

- `toolactivated` fires on `document.modelContext` instead of `window`, and
  aborting the `executeTool()` signal cancels the pending call and fires
  `toolcancel` there. Both are plain `Event` instances with a `toolName` property;
  this package does not define `ToolActivatedEvent` or `ToolCancelEvent`.

  ```diff
  - window.addEventListener('toolactivated', (event) => {
  + document.modelContext?.addEventListener('toolactivated', (event) => {
      console.log(event);
    });
  ```

- Validation failures, unknown or invalid parameters, a missing submit button, and
  rejected responses reject with the generic error described above.

##### Pin webmcp-types to 0.1.9

This package depends on `webmcp-types@0.1.9` exactly. `webmcp-types@0.1.10` adds
required `ontoolactivated` and `ontoolcancel` members plus `ToolActivatedEvent`
and `ToolCancelEvent` globals that the vendored core does not implement, so a
project that also depends on `webmcp-types` must pin the same version until the
runtime catches up:

```bash
pnpm add webmcp-types@0.1.9
```

##### Check the browser baseline

`installWebMCP()` returns without defining `document.modelContext` on engines that
lack an API the vendored core calls, so `if (!document.modelContext)` remains the
feature check. The 5.x polyfill had no such floor.

| API                             | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | ------- | ------ |
| `String.prototype.toWellFormed` | 111    | 119     | 16.4   |
| `AbortSignal.any()`             | 116    | 124     | 17.4   |
| `Promise.withResolvers()`       | 119    | 121     | 17.4   |
| `URL.parse()`                   | 126    | 126     | 18     |

##### Check browser and frame setup

Use a secure page (HTTPS or localhost). Installation preserves existing contexts,
including partial native implementations; it does not upgrade older browser
previews with JSON-string execution. Your browser or supplied context must support
the object-input contract above.

Load the polyfill in every participating frame. Same-origin discovery includes
parents and siblings, so tools can share a name across frames: select the intended
`window`/`origin` and pass the discovered descriptor back to `executeTool()`.
For cross-origin tools, configure the iframe's `tools` permission, the registering
tool's `exposedTo`, and the caller's `getTools({ fromOrigins })`. The vendored
runtime rejects opaque and extension-scheme exposure origins; do not remove origin
restrictions to work around that rejection. See the
[upstream frame setup](https://redirect.github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp-polyfill#frames).

  passes to `respondWith()`. Previously it settled before the form's own `submit`
  listener ran.

  Removing a declarative form after its page called `respondWith()` no longer rejects the
  pending call; it resolves with the response, as in Chrome.

Issues.Title: feat(router): respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by default in `withViewTransitions()`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

---

### Description

`withViewTransitions()` currently triggers a view transition on every router navigation regardless of the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` setting. When the browser supports the View Transitions API, the router always calls `document.startViewTransition()`, and the browser plays at least its default root cross-fade. This happens even for users who have asked their operating system to reduce motion.

Relevant code: [`createViewTransition()` in `packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts). The function decides whether to run `startViewTransition()` based only on browser support (`document.startViewTransition`) and `skipNextTransition`. There is no check against `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.

`prefers-reduced-motion` is not a capability fallback (that part is already handled: unsupported browsers degrade to a plain DOM update). It is a deliberate user accessibility preference, often set for vestibular/motion sensitivity reasons. Treating it as the default opt-out is in line with WCAG guidance (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions) and with how the platform itself frames the preference.

A developer *can* already honor the preference today via the `onViewTransitionCreated` callback and `transition.skipTransition()` (current workaround):

```typescript
withViewTransitions({
  onViewTransitionCreated: ({ transition }) => {
    if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
      transition.skipTransition();
    }
  },
})
```

But this is opt-in boilerplate that most developers won't know they need. The accessible behavior should be the default, following the principle of progressive enhancement: motion is the enhancement layered on top of a working, accessible baseline and not something each team has to remember to switch off.

The View Transitions integration (`withViewTransitions()` / `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`) is still marked `@developerPreview`, so changing the default behavior now carries essentially no ecosystem cost, so IMO now is a good point of time where the default behavior can be changed.

Note: there is a prior related issue, [#52571 — *docs: support prefers-reduced-motion in View Transitions API*](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571), but it was scoped to the angular.dev **website** and closed on the basis that the API already makes it *possible* to respect the preference. This request is different: it asks for the framework to make respecting the preference the **default behavior** of `withViewTransitions()`, not merely possible. A maintainer reference for the mechanism is linked in that thread: [Reacting to the reduced-motion preference (Chrome docs)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions/#reacting-to-the-reduced-motion-preference).

---

### Proposed solution

Make `withViewTransitions()` skip the transition by default when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` is `true`, while still performing the DOM update (the navigation). Concretely, in `createViewTransition()` short-circuit before calling `document.startViewTransition()` when reduced motion is requested — the same way `skipNextTransition` is handled today — so neither Angular's own named transitions nor the browser's default root cross-fade run.

Add an option to `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions` to control this, defaulting to the accessible behavior, e.g.:

```typescript
export interface ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions {
  skipInitialTransition?: boolean;
  onViewTransitionCreated?: (transitionInfo: ViewTransitionInfo) => void;

  /**
   * Whether to skip the view transition when the user has requested reduced
   * motion via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The DOM update (navigation)
   * still runs; only the animation is skipped.
   *
   * @default true
   */
  skipTransitionOnReducedMotion?: boolean;
}
```

- Default `true`: accessible out of the box.
- Teams that have a reason to keep animating (and provide their own reduced-motion-safe animations) can set it to `false`.
- Media-query evaluation should be guarded so it is a no-op on the server / where `matchMedia` is unavailable.

**On the breaking-change question:** this is a behavior change, but a small and
defensible one, and arguably a bug fix rather than a breaking change:

- The API is `@developerPreview`, so it is explicitly not covered by SemVer stability guarantees.
- The current behavior arguably violates the user's expressed accessibility preference, so changing it is closer to fixing a defect than removing a feature.
- The visible effect of the new default only materializes for users who have `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set — i.e. exactly the users who asked for less motion.

---

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep it opt-in via `onViewTransitionCreated` (status quo).** Works, but leaves the accessible behavior as hidden boilerplate most teams never add, so real apps ship motion to users who opted out. Rejected as the default.

2. **Conditionally register `withViewTransitions()` at bootstrap** by checking `prefers-reduced-motion` first (mirrors the old `NoopAnimationsModule`/`BrowserAnimationsModule` split suggested in [#52571](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571)). This reads the preference only once at startup and does not react to changes, requires the developer to wire it up, and spreads config logic into bootstrap. Less ergonomic than a sensible default.

3. **Document the `onViewTransitionCreated` + `skipTransition()` pattern only, without changing the default.** Better than nothing, but documentation does not change the default experience; accessibility defaults should be safe, not something you read your way into.

4. **CSS-only mitigation** (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` around all custom keyframes). This disables the author's own animations but does **not** stop the browser's default root cross-fade that `startViewTransition()` triggers, so motion still reaches the user. It is a complement, not a substitute, for skipping the transition at the API level.

---

### Willing to contribute

I'd be happy to work on this myself and open a PR (changes to `createViewTransition()` and `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`, plus tests and docs). Before I start, I'd like to confirm with the team whether the proposed direction — making reduced-motion skipping the default, with an opt-out option — is acceptable, and whether you'd prefer a different API shape or naming. Happy to adjust based on your guidance.

Issues.Title: test(compiler-cli): migrate compliance test expectations to full-file goldens
Issues.Body:
## Summary
Migrates the `ngtsc` compliance test suite from snippet-based golden files to full-file golden files and removes the duplicate `normalizeJsForComparison` helpers from `packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/test/compliance_spec.ts`.

### Changes
- **Full-file Golden Files**: Expanded macro calls (`__AttributeMarker`, `__SelectorFlags`, `__QueryFlags`, `__i18nMsg__`) and `$...$` identifier placeholders in compliance golden files to full-file `ngtsc` output, using `…` only where partial-linker output legitimately diverges (`r3_view_compiler_deferred/deferred_with_duplicate_external_dep_template.js`, `r3_view_compiler_i18n/line_ending_normalization/*_template_non_legacy_*.js`, and `r3_compiler_compliance/ng_modules/providers{,.local}.js`). Kept `source_mapping/` golden files (`// SOURCE:` comments) intact.
- **Consolidated Expectations**: Merged the 29 multi-snippet test cases in `TEST_CASES.json` (preserving all `extraChecks`) into single full-file expectations per generated `.js` file and removed the 78 redundant snippet files. Un-shared the 3 shared snippet files in `r3_view_compiler_i18n/line_ending_normalization/TEST_CASES.json` so each test case has its own full-file golden.
- **Explicitly Scoped `expectEmit` Normalizations**:
  - Updated `expectEmit` to sub-chunk large token arrays and string literals so full-file goldens stay within V8's `RegExp` size limit, and updated `stripLineComments` to ignore `//` inside string/template literals.
  - Explicitly scoped partial-linker normalizations (`ɵsetClassDebugInfo` / `ɵɵsetNgModuleScope` elision and linked `MSG_...` constant names) behind `options.isLinkedCompilation` so `full compile` and `local compile` (`ngtsc`) assert the full unstripped output.
  - Explicitly scoped NGP emit normalizations behind `isNgpTestMode() || options?.isNgpCompilation`.
- **Consolidated NGP Emit Normalizations**: Consolidated NGP-specific cosmetic normalizations into `normalizeNgpEmitForComparison` (`packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/testing/src/ngp_emit_normalizer.ts`) and removed the duplicate `normalizeJsForComparison` helpers from `packages/compiler-cli/preprocessor/test/compliance_spec.ts`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): coalesce external watcher directories to avoid macOS FSEvents limit
Issues.Body:
Previously, `ParcelExternalManager` immediately created a separate `@parcel/watcher` subscription for the parent directory of every watched file outside the workspace root. In monorepo setups where an application imports from hundreds of external library directories and hoisted `node_modules` packages, this exceeded macOS's ~512 per-process `FSEvents` stream limit, causing subsequent subscriptions to silently fail and miss file changes.

To prevent exhausting native watcher streams, `ParcelExternalManager` now normalizes external `node_modules` file paths to their package root directory and batches synchronous file additions and removals within a microtask so nested child directories are subsumed before subscribing. When the number of external target directories exceeds the subscription budget of 256, a prefix tree is used to iteratively collapse the deepest branching subdirectories into common ancestors while preferring directories that do not contain `workspaceRoot`. Additionally, if `parcelWatcher.subscribe()` rejects for an existing directory on disk, the manager dynamically lowers its subscription budget and re-reconciles into higher-level ancestor directories.

Closes #34246

When `rootFiles` overrides are provided (such as during `unit-test` runs), the initial TypeScript program is restricted to those entry points and their transitive imports. If a test imports a non-standalone `@Component` directly without importing its declaring `@NgModule`, the `NgModule` may be omitted from the program and leave the component without its compilation scope.

Preserve the full `tsconfig` root file set as `fallbackRootNames` for application builds when `rootFiles` is a subset of the `tsconfig` files. If AOT analysis detects a non-standalone component lacking an owning `NgModule` scope (`getOwningNgModule(component) === null`) and additional uncompiled `tsconfig` files exist, recreate and re-analyze the Angular program with the full root file set so all `NgModule` declarations can be discovered.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular-devkit/schematics): avoid stack overflow when chaining many rules
Issues.Body:

- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

`chain()` builds one nested observable per rule. With a few thousand rules, subscribing to the result goes past the call stack limit. Locally, 2000 no-op rules gave a promise that never settled, and the issue reports `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

Issue Number: #17851

## What is the new behavior?

`chain()` awaits each rule's result before calling the next rule, so the stack depth no longer grows with the number of rules. The new spec in `base_spec.ts` chains 20000 rules. It times out on main and passes with this change.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Tested with `bazel test //packages/angular_devkit/schematics/... //packages/schematics/angular:test //packages/angular_devkit/schematics_cli/...`.

Closes #17851

Issues.Title: unit-test builder (Vitest): test bundle output is not deterministic, which defeats Vitest 5 `fsModuleCache`
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Building the same project twice in a row with `@angular/build:unit-test` (Vitest runner), with no source change in between, produces different output files: the same modules end up with different chunk names, because the import statements inside some chunks and spec entry points come out in a different order.

Only the order changes, never the code. Normalising the chunk names (`chunk-[A-Z0-9]{8}` → `chunk-X`) and comparing the files, every difference is one of:

- side-effect imports reordered in a spec entry point:
  ```diff
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  ```
- named imports moved between two `import { … } from "./chunk-X.js"` statements:
  ```diff
  +import {
  +  SomeMapper
  +} from "./chunk-X.js";
   ...
  -import {
  -  SomeMapper
  -} from "./chunk-X.js";
  ```
- identifiers swapped in a re-exported list (`ModuleA, ModuleB` → `ModuleB, ModuleA`).

Since the chunk file names are content hashes, one reordered chunk renames itself and, in cascade, every chunk or spec that imports it.

Measured on two applications of the same workspace (two consecutive `ng test <app> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`):

| project | JS files in the test bundle | files renamed between two runs |
|---|---|---|
| app A, JIT test build (`aot: false`) | 593 | 79 to 89 |
| app B, JIT test build | 89 | 10 |
| app B, AOT (default `build:development`) | 88 | 18 |
| two small libraries | 9 and 11 | 0 |

It happens with and without `--coverage`, in AOT and JIT, and with `NG_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS=1`, so it does not look like a worker race in the Angular compilation.

**Why it matters.** Vitest 5 enables `fsModuleCache` by default and keys it on file content and id. With the builder's output changing between runs, part of the cache is invalidated on every run (about 20 % of the entries for app A), so the cache cannot be reused between CI pipelines. Disabling `splitting` makes the output stable (100 % cache reuse) but the option is deprecated ("No longer needed with Vitest 5") and the suite is much slower without shared chunks (app A with coverage, warm cache: ~45 s instead of ~30 s).

Expected: identical inputs give byte-identical test bundles, as they would for a reproducible build.

### Minimal Reproduction

Not yet reduced to a public repository. Any workspace whose specs share enough code to produce many shared chunks should show it:

1. `ng test <project> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`
2. Copy `.angular/cache/<version>/<project>/unit-test/output-files` aside.
3. Run step 1 again, without touching anything.
4. Compare the two lists of `*.js` file names: some chunk names differ. Diffing a renamed chunk against its counterpart only shows reordered imports.

Small projects (around ten output files) do not show it in our workspace.

### Exception or Error

_No response_

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64 (on the node:24-alpine CI image, the persisted Vitest cache also grows on every pipeline instead of being reused)

@angular/build    : 22.2.2
vitest            : 5.0.4
esbuild           : 0.28.2
typescript        : 6.0.3
```

Unit-test target: `@angular/build:unit-test`, Vitest runner, jsdom, `isolate: false`, v8 coverage.

### Anything else relevant?

Related but distinct: #31724 (unit-test builder slow for testing and coverage). A deterministic test bundle would let `fsModuleCache` be persisted between CI runs, which would help there.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "unit-test builder (Vitest): test bundle output is not deterministic, which defeats Vitest 5 `fsModuleCache`" (#34335)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): sort discovered unit-test files for deterministic builds
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #34335

`findTests` returns the test files in the order `tinyglobby` yields them. The glob crawls directories asynchronously, so the order changes between runs: on a project with 255 spec files, 8 consecutive calls returned 8 different orders (same set of files). That order feeds the build entry points and `rootFiles`, so two `ng test` builds of the same sources produce different chunks: imports come out reordered, the content-hashed chunk names change, and the change cascades to every importer (79 to 89 of 593 output files renamed between two runs). This defeats Vitest 5's `fsModuleCache`, which is keyed on file content.

## What is the new behavior?

The discovered test files are sorted before being turned into entry points. With that change, three consecutive builds of the same project produced byte-identical test bundles (0 of 593 files differing, `--dump-virtual-files` output compared with `diff -r`), and Vitest's module cache was fully reused across runs.

A `findTests` spec checks the result is sorted. The crawl order can happen to be sorted on a small fixture, so it guards against a regression rather than reproducing the race on every run.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Measured with `@angular/build` 22.2.2, Vitest 5.0.4, Node 24, on macOS; the same non-determinism shows up in AOT and JIT test builds, with and without `--coverage`, and with `NG_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS=1`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve incremental .d.ts signatures and emit state in watch mode
Issues.Body:
- Drain newly created `.ngtypecheck.ts` shims after `collectDiagnostics()` using `emitNextAffectedFile` with `isolatedModules` and `assumeChangesOnlyAffectDirectDependencies` enabled so TypeScript does not walk `referencedMap` from `.ngtypecheck.ts` shims to component `.ts` files and their transitive importers, preserving their `.d.ts` shape signatures and keeping `affectedFilesPendingEmit` clean for the next watch rebuild.
- Ensure `before` transformers (`ivyTransformFactory`) have executed on the original `SourceFile` prior to `afterDeclarations` (`declarationTransformFactory`) when TypeScript performs a `.d.ts`-only emit (`emitOnly = Dts`) for transitive importers.
- Avoid marking a `SourceFile` as having completed JS emit in `writeFileCallback` when only a `.d.ts` or `.map` file was emitted during a `.d.ts`-only check, and pass `ts.EmitOnly.Js` in the fallback loop when `.d.ts` was already emitted.
- Track transitive importers whose `BuilderProgram` shape signatures are reset to `sourceFile.version` by `handleDtsMayChangeOf` during `findAffectedFiles()` so `populatePreviousDtsSignatures()` restores their `.d.ts` signatures if they are modified on a subsequent rebuild.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): preserve preload metadata for nested empty-path routes
Issues.Body:
Previously, `handleRoute` yielded a parent route's metadata before appending `loadChildren` preloads or traversing child routes, while `traverseRoutesConfig` appended a trailing slash only to empty-path routes. Under a non-empty parent, the parent ('/pricing') and its empty-path child ('/pricing/') received distinct keys during `getRoutesFromAngularRouterConfig` deduplication (`seenRoutes`) and were only merged later by `RouteTree.insert`. However, when an empty-path route was nested under another empty-path route (such as at the root '/' or under '/es' -> '' -> ''), both the parent and child received the same key, causing `seenRoutes` to keep the outer route's metadata and drop the descendant's accumulated `preload` and redirect metadata.

Update `handleRoute` to append `loadChildren` preloads upfront and allow the first matching empty-path child route to override its parent's metadata for the same path, and remove the redundant `addTrailingSlash` keying in `traverseRoutesConfig`.

Closes #34320

#### 🐞 Bug fixes

- Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by [@​YuryShkoda](https://redirect.github.com/YuryShkoda) in [#​4893](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/4893)

  Fixed the behavior of `res.send()` to prevent conflicts between `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` HTTP headers in responses. The `Content-Length` header in `res.send()` is now only added when a `Transfer-Encoding` header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a `Transfer-Encoding` header - by [@​cuishuang](https://redirect.github.com/cuishuang) in [#​7459](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7459)

* Upgrade `qs` to `^6.16.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-2391](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-2391) ([GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883](https://redirect.github.com/ljharb/qs/security/advisories/GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883)), [CVE-2026-82417](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82417) ([GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g)) and [CVE-2026-82562](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82562) ([GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx)): `arrayLimit` bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled `isBuffer` - by [@​davetashner](https://redirect.github.com/davetashner) in [#​7057](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7057) and [#​7478](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7478), and [@​cyphercodes](https://redirect.github.com/cyphercodes) in [#​7305](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7305)

* Upgrade `proxy-addr` to `^2.0.8`, which fixes [CVE-2026-90711](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-90711) - by [@​lazerg](https://redirect.github.com/lazerg) in [#​7474](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7474)

#### 🚀 Improvements

- Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. `req.fresh` previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by [@​Cherry](https://redirect.github.com/Cherry) in [#​7366](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7366)

  ```js

    res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
    res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
  ```

- When calling `app.render` with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by [AkaHarshit](https://redirect.github.com/AkaHarshit) in [#​6903](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/6903)

  ```js
  app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected
  ```

- Upgrade `content-type` to `^2.0.0`, bringing a faster parser (\~1.5x quicker `Content-Type` parsing/formatting in `res.send()`) along with a behavior change: `res.send()` now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a `Content-Type` that fails to parse. `type-is` is upgraded to `^2.1.0` as part of the same change - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7234](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7234)

  ```js
  res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
  // -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8
  ```

This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by [@​blakeembrey](https://redirect.github.com/blakeembrey) in [#​7233](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7233)

  ```js
  res.attachment('user.html');
  // before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
  // after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html
  ```

- Upgrade `body-parser` to `^2.3.0`, which fixes [CVE-2026-12590](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-12590) ([GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/body-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)): an invalid `limit` option value caused request body size enforcement to be silently disabled (fail-open), allowing a denial of service via arbitrarily large payloads. Invalid `limit` values now throw at parser initialization instead of being ignored - by [@​Mayvis](https://redirect.github.com/Mayvis) in [#​7390](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/pull/7390)

### [`v12.11.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.2): pnpm 12.11.2

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.1...v12.11.2)

This release fixes `--workspace-concurrency=Infinity`, filters set by an `updateConfig` hook, and store fetches with `enable-modules-dir=false`.

##### Patch Changes

- `--workspace-concurrency=Infinity` now runs workspace projects with no concurrency limit. It used to fail with `invalid digit found in string` [#​16793](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16793).

- `enable-modules-dir=false` now also fetches the packages an install reuses from an existing lockfile, so the store holds every package the lockfile lists.

### [`v12.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.11.1): pnpm 12.11.1

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.11.0...v12.11.1)

This release fixes two ways `pnpm install` could fail, runs tools of any Rust release through `pnx`, and treats `registry.npmjs.com` as an alias of the npm registry.

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm install` no longer fails when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version. pnpm warns and continues. A registry mirror that has not synced a release no longer blocks the commands of a project pinned to it.

- `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD` when `node_modules/.bin` holds a shim that another user created, if everyone can already execute it and it is not world-writable. This happens when several users share one checkout.

- `enable-modules-dir=false` (`enableModulesDir: false` through the Node.js addon) fetches the registry packages the host can install into the store again, as pnpm v10 did, while still writing nothing under `node_modules`. The setting exists for a `node_modules` that something else mounts from the store, such as a FUSE daemon, and that consumer no longer has to download each package on first access. A plain `--lockfile-only` run still fetches nothing.

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer put `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` files in the tarball. A `files` entry that names one still ships it.

- pnpm now treats `https://registry.npmjs.com/` as an alias of `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Registry requests, credentials, and trusted publishing use the canonical hostname.

- `pnx --package=rust@<channel> <tool>` runs a tool of that Rust release, for example `pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-01-01 cargo build`. pnpm installs the release with the components and targets from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the target of each `--target` argument.

- `pnpm install` now links agent skills for more coding agents. It detects the agent from `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `AI_AGENT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE` [pnpm/tasks#116](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/116).

- When the registry rejects `pnpm stage publish`, the error message now starts with "Failed to stage package".

Issues.Title: build: fix API docs extraction of directives and imported types
Issues.Body:
The ARIA and CDK API pages on angular.dev are missing information, because the API extraction can't resolve several imports:

- 8 aria directives are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties, because their host directives are imported from another package.
- The drag-drop target doesn't use the import map, so `@angular/core` doesn't resolve, and its imports of other cdk packages aren't available. Most of its directives and its NgModule are shown as classes, and their inputs and outputs as plain properties.
- Many types are shown as `any`.

The extraction doesn't report any of this, because it ignores Angular compilation errors.

## Changes

Extraction rule:
- Map an import map entry to its target's own entry point, and fail if it doesn't exist. Currently, the rule picks the shortest `index.d.ts` among the target and its dependencies, which maps `@angular/aria/private` to `src/cdk/platform/index.d.ts`.
- Resolve relative imports of files outside `srcs` to the type declarations among the inputs, by setting `rootDirs` to include the bin directory. This mirrors how `ts_project` sees sources and declarations. A new `deps` attribute provides declarations that the import map doesn't.
- Map wildcards of directory entries relative to the directory itself, so that subpath imports like `rxjs/operators` resolve.
- Treat missing compiled stylesheets as empty, since they aren't inputs of the action and don't affect the docs.
- Fail on Angular compilation errors.

Targets: all of them use the wrapper with the import map, and those with relative imports of other packages (aria, drag-drop and three cdk/testing targets) get `deps`.

## Effect on the generated docs

Compared with `main`, 46 of the 110 aria and cdk API pages change:
- 13 classes are shown as directives and one as an NgModule, and their inputs and outputs as such, e.g. `readonly id = input<string>()` instead of `readonly id: InputSignal<any>`, or `@Input('cdkDragData') data: T` instead of `data: T`.
- Types shown as `any` show their real type, e.g. `Signal<boolean>` instead of `Signal<any>`, or `Subject<{ source: DragRef<any>; event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent; }>` instead of `any` for `DragRef.started`.
- Members inherited from base classes that now resolve are listed.
- The `Combobox` page no longer links `DeferredContentAware` to `/api/aria/private/DeferredContentAware`, which doesn't exist.

No page or member is removed, and no type gets worse. The remaining `any`s are declared as such in the source.

## Testing

- Every docs target builds on `main` and on each commit. Comparing all fields of the generated JSON, each commit only changes what its message describes.
- Each fix is needed: removing it brings its errors or `any`s back. Moving the remaining cdk/testing targets to the wrapper and removing the unused import map entry don't change the output, and neither does the stricter entry point for the remaining import map entries, which already resolve to their own entry point.
- `bazel build //...`, `pnpm lint` and the aria/combobox unit tests pass.

Issues.Title: bug(mat-datepicker): date parse errors are not propagated to Signal Forms
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The datepicker input provides a matDatepickerParse validation error when the user enters text that cannot be parsed as a date.

This error is available when using Reactive Forms, but when using Signal Forms, the error does not reach the errors signal of the field tree. The value of the form field stays as `null`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-d3y2q7gw?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the application.
2. Enter an invalid date string into the Reactive Forms datepicker.
3. Observe that the control reports a matDatepickerParse error.
4. Enter the same invalid date string into the Signal Forms datepicker.
5. Observe that the Signal Forms field does not report the corresponding parse error in field().errors().

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the date parse errors to also be available to the Signal Form.

If I understand correctly, this seems to be in line with the direction of the Angular Signal Forms API, for example with https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/transformedValue to report parse errors in custom controls.

### Actual Behavior

The date parse errors are not available to the Signal Form. Since the form value remains as `null` for invalid values, distinguishing between an empty form and invalid input is not possible in the schema.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.2
- CDK/Material: 22.2.2
- Browser(s): Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): update parse error with signal forms when value stays null
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33740.

When a datepicker input is bound to a signal form with `[formField]`, the `matDatepickerParse` error goes stale whenever the model value stays `null`:

- typing an unparseable value (e.g. `foo`) into an empty input does not add the error;
- erasing an unparseable value does not clear it, so the form stays invalid on an empty field (the case in the issue).

## Cause

Signal forms compute the errors of a CVA's legacy validators in a `computed` that re-runs when the control value changes or when the validator calls its `registerOnValidatorChange` callback. In `MatDatepickerInputBase._onInput()`, the `null` to `null` path calls `_cvaOnChange(null)`, which signal forms ignore because the value did not change, and it never calls `_validatorOnChange()`: that call was only in the branch for a non-null, unchanged date. Reactive forms don't hit this, because `setValue` always re-runs the validators.

## Fix

Call `_validatorOnChange()` whenever the parse state flips while the value stays the same, including `null` to `null`. The branch that already did this for an unchanged non-null date behaves as before.

With reactive forms, the `null` to `null` case with a changed parse state now also triggers `updateValueAndValidity()` after the `setValue(null)` call. It gives the same result, with one extra `valueChanges`/`statusChanges` emission in that case.

## Testing

Two tests in `datepicker.spec.ts` use a real signal form (`form()` + `FormField`). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- typing `foo` into an empty input sets `matDatepickerParse`;
- setting a date, typing `foo`, then clearing the input removes it.

`//src/material/datepicker:unit_tests_chromium` (407 tests, including the date range input) and `//src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium` pass locally.

Issues.Title: bug(COMPONENT): Angular ARIA tab must allow eager loading of tab content
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

## Description

Angular Aria's tabs implementation appears to require tab panel content to be declared using `ng-template[ngTabContent]`, which prevents consumers from eagerly rendering tab panel content in the DOM.

This is problematic for use cases where all tab panels need to be initialized upfront, rather than lazily instantiated when their associated tabs become active. For example, a tab panel may contain a component that needs to initialize early, or preload data that is required for SEO (in SSR setup).

Currently, `ngTabContent` can only be applied to an `ng-template`, and the implementation warns when a tab panel does not contain the expected content directive. Applying `ngTabContent` directly to a component or a regular element does not work because it does not match the directive's selector.

It would be useful to provide a supported way to eagerly instantiate tab panel content while retaining the existing tab panel API and accessibility behavior.

## Reasoning

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide recommends automatic tab activation on focus when the associated panel can be displayed without noticeable latency. It also notes that this typically requires panel content to be preloaded; otherwise, automatic activation introduces delays that significantly hinder efficient keyboard navigation.

Eager loading is therefore a legitimate use case for accessible tabs, particularly when panel content requires initialization or data fetching before it can be displayed.

Providing an explicit mechanism for eager content instantiation would allow developers to avoid unnecessary delays during tab navigation without having to implement their own tab behavior or work around the current content directive requirements.

### Reproduction

Link: https://angular.dev/guide/aria/tabs#example-1



### Expected Behavior

I expect the ngTabContent to have a selector on its own without the ng-template infront, so that the tab content can be eagerly loaded

### Actual Behavior

The ngTabContent selector has ng-template in front of it which prevents us from eagerly loading tab content that may contain useful information and is needed upfront and without layout shift

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: N/A
- Browser(s): latest
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A

Issues.Title: fix(google-maps): avoid inline host style that violates CSP style-src
Issues.Body:
## What

`MapInfoWindow` hides its host element with `host: {'style': 'display: none'}`. This renders as an inline `style` attribute on `<map-info-window>`, which is blocked by a Content Security Policy whose `style-src` doesn't include `'unsafe-inline'`. The browser reports a violation like this for every info window on the page:

> Applying inline style violates the following Content Security Policy directive 'style-src ...'

## Fix

Remove the host style binding and set `display: none` on the host element in the constructor through CSSOM (`element.style.display`). CSP doesn't block CSSOM assignments, so the behavior is unchanged and the directive works under a strict `style-src`.

## Testing

Verified in an app running a strict CSP (`style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'`): before the change, each `<map-info-window>` raised a CSP violation; after it, none are raised, and the info windows still open and close normally.

Issues.Title: bug(cdk/text-field): cdkTextareaAutosize caches line height before matInput applies `font: inherit`, so min/max rows are wrong
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

14.x (verified on v14.material.angular.dev, Angular 14.0.0)

### Description

When `cdkTextareaAutosize` is used on a `matInput` textarea inside `mat-form-field`, the cached line height used for `cdkAutosizeMinRows` / `cdkAutosizeMaxRows` is measured with the browser's default textarea font instead of the form field's font. As a result, `min-height` / `max-height` are too small until the window is resized.

**Cause (as far as I can tell):**
- `CdkTextareaAutosize` measures and caches the line height on the first `ngDoCheck` (`resizeToFitContent` → `_cacheTextareaLineHeight`, cloning the textarea with `rows=1`).
- `MatInput` applies `font: inherit` via the class `mat-mdc-form-field-input-control`, which is a *dynamic* host binding (`'[class.mat-mdc-form-field-input-control]': '_isInFormField'`).
- Host bindings are applied after `ngDoCheck` in the first change detection pass. So at measuring time the textarea (and its clone) still uses the UA default textarea font (Chrome: monospace 13.33px, `line-height: normal` ≈ 15px).
- The wrong value stays cached until a window `resize` clears it.

**Measured on the official docs example** (`cdkAutosizeMaxRows="5"`, actual line height 24px):

| Docs | Angular | measured line height | `max-height` |
|---|---|---|---|
| v14 | 14.0.0 | 18px (correct) | 90px |
| v15 | 15.1.1 | 15px | 75px |
| v17 | 17.3.0 | 15px | 75px |
| v19 | 19.2.6 | 15px | 75px |
| v21 | 21.2.11 | 15px | 75px |
| current | 22.2.1 | 15px | 75px (expected 120px) |

It started with v15, i.e. the switch to the MDC-based form field.

**Workaround:** a global style so the textarea inherits the font before the first measurement:
```css
textarea.cdk-textarea-autosize { font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; }
```

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz needed – the official docs example reproduces it:
https://material.angular.dev/cdk/text-field/examples ("Auto-resizing textarea")

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open the page above (fresh load, don't resize the window).
2. Select the textarea in DevTools and run:
   ```js
   ({ minHeight: $0.style.minHeight, maxHeight: $0.style.maxHeight, lineHeight: getComputedStyle($0).lineHeight })
   ```
   → `minHeight: "15px"`, `maxHeight: "75px"`, `lineHeight: "24px"`
3. Type more than 3 lines: the textarea starts scrolling after ~3 lines instead of 5.
4. Resize the browser window and run the snippet again → `minHeight: "24px"`, `maxHeight: "120px"` (correct).

For comparison, the same example on https://v14.material.angular.dev/cdk/text-field/examples measures correctly on first load.

### Expected Behavior

min-height / max-height are based on the actual line height of the textarea (24px → max-height: 120px for 5 rows) right after the first render.

### Actual Behavior

They are based on the UA default textarea font (15px → max-height: 75px) until the window is resized.

### Environment

- Angular 22.2.1
- CDK/Material 22.2.x
- Chrome (Version 154.0.8037.95 (64-Bit))
- Windows 11

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.28.2` → `11.28.5`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.28.2/11.28.5?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.5`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.5): pnpm 11.28.5 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.4...v11.28.5) This release reads cached registry metadata faster and makes `pnpm config get --global` ignore project settings. It also carries several security fixes for package archives, git dependencies, and config dependencies. ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - pnpm now verifies locked config dependencies against their registry before installing them. Config dependencies must come from an npm registry. The lockfile can no longer replace the integrity of a config dependency pinned with `version+integrity`. - Lockfile verification now checks the tarballs inside a `variations` resolution against the registry. A `name@version` lockfile entry with an empty `variations` resolution is now rejected. - `pnpm audit signatures` now verifies signatures against the integrity recorded in the lockfile. Packages without a recorded integrity cannot pass signature verification. - pnpm now rejects a git dependency whose lockfile repository is empty, begins with `-`, or contains a null byte. Git can no longer read such a value as a command-line option [pnpm/tasks#84](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/84). - A git dependency with a `#path:` subpath can no longer reach files outside the repository through a symlink in the subpath. - `pnpm pack`, `pnpm publish`, and installs of git and local directory dependencies now leave out files that a directory symlink or a `bundleDependencies` entry points to outside the package directory [pnpm/tasks#83](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/83) [pnpm/tasks#93](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/93). - `pnpm deploy` with `deployAllFiles` now rejects symlinks that point outside the package directory. Local package installs with this setting apply the same check. - pnpm no longer hangs on a package archive with a negative PAX record length or an entry of 4 GiB or more [pnpm/tasks#78](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/78) [pnpm/tasks#79](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/79). - Large package downloads and large files inside gzip and bzip2 package archives now use bounded memory during installation. Package manifests and archive metadata larger than 64 MiB are rejected. `pnpm publish` also rejects manifests and README files larger than 64 MiB in pre-built tarballs before reading them into memory. - Two URL or local path dependencies no longer share a virtual store directory when one URL has `+`, `#`, `:`, or `?` where the other has `/`. Such dependencies, including git dependencies pinned with `#`, now get a hash suffix on their directory name. - `pnpm licenses` now removes terminal control characters from package metadata in table output. - The warnings about ignored project `.npmrc` registry and auth settings no longer print the username and password of a URL-scoped key such as `//user:password@registry.example.com/:_authToken`. ##### Installing and resolving dependencies - Dependency resolution reads cached registry metadata faster. The metadata cache moved to `/v12/`, so the first install after upgrading downloads registry metadata again. A damaged cache entry is downloaded again, or reported as an error when `--offline` is set [#​13512](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13512). - `pnpm install` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a dependency uses a specifier with a protocol pnpm does not support, such as Yarn's `patch:`. pnpm linked such a dependency to a directory that does not exist [#​16590](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16590). - When a dependency moves an exact dependency of its own to an older version, a peer dependency that pnpm installed automatically now moves with it. Before, `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` kept the newer locked version of the peer, so the lockfile held two copies of it, for example two copies of `vue` [pnpm/tasks#61](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/61). - `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now keep the peer dependencies that `pnpm-lock.yaml` records for a package they did not update. A registry whose metadata disagrees with the package's `package.json`, for example by omitting `peerDependenciesMeta`, made `pnpm add` and `pnpm dedupe` write different lockfiles, so `pnpm dedupe --check` failed after `pnpm add` [#​16615](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16615). ##### Configuration - `pnpm config get` and `pnpm config list` with `--global` or `--location=global` now show only the global configuration. Both flags included the project's `.npmrc` before. `--location=global` also included the project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `pnpm config get --global` failed when the global bin directory was not in PATH [#​16598](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16598). - pnpm now prints config warnings, such as an unset environment variable in `.npmrc`, when loading the config fails. - pnpm now fails when `httpProxy` or `httpsProxy` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global configuration is not a string. - `pnpm dlx` now uses the `release` entry of `nodeDownloadMirrors` from the workspace configuration when downloading Node.js runtimes [#​11281](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11281). Mirrors for other channels, such as `rc` and `nightly`, still apply only from the global configuration. ##### Commands - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now forward `--config.*` command-line flags to the install started by `verifyDepsBeforeRun` [pnpm/tasks#60](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/60). - `pnpm dlx` with `--package` but no command now fails with `'pnpm dlx' requires a command to run`. Before, it installed the package and then crashed trying to run an empty command. - `pnpm unpublish @` now deletes the tarball under the registry's path when the registry is served under one, such as Gitea's npm registry. It used to send the delete to the host root and report success without removing the version [#​16568](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16568). It also no longer mistakes a sibling path such as `/npm-mirror/` for the registry path `/npm/` [pnpm/tasks#94](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/94). - The interactive `pnpm audit --fix` picker now shows each patched version with the `saveExact` and `savePrefix` style that the override is written with [#​13209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13209). - `pnpm list` now reports the correct package paths when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​9593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9593). - `pnpm setup` now puts `$PNPM_HOME/bin` first on `PATH` in login shells that inherited it further down, such as the VS Code terminal on macOS. Before, another `node` took precedence over the one installed by `pnpm runtime set node -g`. Run `pnpm setup` again to update the block in your shell config [#​16635](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16635). - `pnpm setup` now names the shell config file even if it is already up to date [#​16608](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16608). ##### Output and messages - A warning about a project's `devEngines` or `packageManager` pin is now printed to stderr. A command such as `pnpm cache path` or `pnpm list --json` keeps only its own output on stdout [#​16584](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16584). - The warning for a non-root `resolutions` field now points at the `overrides` field in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​11757](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/11757). #### Platinum Sponsors
